The 3-Point Fit Checklist: Will a Straight Stair Lift Work for You?

Stand at the bottom of your stairs and answer three questions. If you can say yes to all three, a straight stair lift is very likely the right fit.

1 Do your stairs run in one straight line from bottom to top?

No turns, no curve, and no landing where the stairs change direction. A straight run is what lets us use a standard rail that's cut to length, which is why the price is lower and the install is quick.

Have a flat landing in the middle? You may still qualify with two straight lifts.

2 Are all the steps the same rectangular shape?

Pie-shaped or triangular steps (called winders) mean the staircase turns, even if it looks nearly straight. Those need a custom curved rail.

3 Can the rider sit down and stand up safely at the top and bottom?

The rider needs to be able to sit upright, and to get on and off the seat with or without a helper. The seat swivels at the top so you step off onto the floor, not onto the stairs. Most stair lifts need about 28 to 30 inches of stair width, and slim-rail models can sometimes fit narrower stairs.

Three yeses? You're a great fit.

Call (586) 999-9042 or send the form and we'll confirm it with a free home assessment.

Get My Free Assessment

Not sure, or answered no to one? Send us two photos of your staircase. We'll tell you honestly what will work, including when a straight lift isn't the right answer.

Why straight

Why a Straight Stair Lift Is the Smart Choice

Fast

Straight rails are stocked in standard lengths and cut to fit your stairs. Installation typically takes two to four hours.

Non-invasive

The rail is fastened to the stair treads. Nothing is cut into the wall, and the stairs can be restored if the lift is removed.

Affordable

No custom fabrication means a much lower price than a curved lift. Starting at $X,XXX fully installed.

Still your staircase

The seat, arms and footrest fold up, leaving room for everyone else to walk the stairs.

Independence, Without Changing Your Home

A stair lift isn't a renovation. There's no construction dust and no crew in the house for a week. You sit, fasten the belt, press the control and ride. Your bedroom stays your bedroom.

✓ Simple control on the armrest
✓ Swivel seat for a safe step-off at the top
✓ Seat belt and obstruction sensors
✓ Runs on battery power, so it works during a power outage [CONFIRM]

Peace of Mind for Sons, Daughters and Caregivers

Falls on stairs are one of the biggest worries for anyone caring for an aging parent. We make the fix simple: one company to call, a firm price before work starts, and a lift that's in and working in days.

✓ Written price up front, with nothing added later
✓ Coordinated with hospital or rehab discharge dates
✓ A whole-home safety look while we're there

Straight Stair Lift FAQ

How long does straight stair lift installation take?

Typically two to four hours once the lift is on site. From first call to a working lift is usually a matter of days.

Does the rail attach to the wall?

No. It attaches to the stair treads, so walls and railings are left alone.

Can other people still use the stairs?

Yes. The seat, arms and footrest fold up when the lift isn't in use.

What if the power goes out?

How much weight can a stair lift carry?

Not at all. See how two straight lifts can replace one custom curved lift.
